orderingRuling.standing: DELIVERY's to make and made here. IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md section 6 law 19 assigns the identity to DELIVERY; whether a capability manifest's collections carry meaning in their order is a fact about DELIVERY's data model. An independent review proved the question was open and load-bearing; a recipe candidate correctly declined to answer it. This section answers it.

JSON's own reading of an array is a sequence.

Both encodings this identity could use already state that the DEFAULT IS NOT SILENT and that the owning surface must DECLARE, and both provide the mechanism for declaring. What was missing was DELIVERY's declaration, not a rule.

CVE1 therefore ALREADY CARRIES a set-declaration mechanism, and using it is not invention. This ruling is DELIVERY supplying the field-specific rule that sentence requires and DELIVERY never wrote.
whereTheRuleComesFrom.leg2_theSAMESURFACEDOESITFORTHEANALOGOUS: resolved-inputs.v2#planIdContract.fieldCanonicalization.semanticUniverses, verbatim: 'Sort by providerId UTF-8 bytes; providerId is unique.' That is a PROVIDER LIST, in the very identity capabilityManifestId feeds, declared a key-sorted unique set by its owner. And .scope, verbatim: 'workspaceUnitIds and requestedPaths are sorted unique NFC UTF-8 strings' -- an identifier-string list, declared a sorted unique set. Both shapes recur exactly inside CapabilityManifestV1, and this ruling gives them the same treatment their owner gave them one level up.
whereTheRuleComesFrom.leg3_theOTHERCANDIDATEENCODINGSAYSTHESAM: evaluation-proof.v8#normativePreimageGrammar.recordRules states BOTH halves: sortedLists ('sort complete item record bytes ... ascending before item framing') and programOrder ('PolicyV2.evaluationOrder preserves the declared program order and is not sorted'). One NAMED field is exempt and everything else sorts. The discipline is identical in both encodings: order-bearing is NAMED, never inferred.

An order-significant providers array would commit a provider ordering INTO PlanId, which that sentence forbids in the same contract. IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md section 6 law 3 says the same thing from the architecture side: strength is a property of a predicate and its Coverage, not of a tier, and there is no rank to compare.

Uniqueness is not an extra: a manifest that names one providerId twice makes two capability claims about one provider and its relations map stops being a function.

perFieldRuling.rationale: an ordering of absences has no referent: there is no first absence. IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md section 6 law 4 requires every required predicate to receive EXACT Coverage and forbids unmet requiredness becoming a pass or a false no-match -- which makes an absent-coverage entry a per-(provider, relation) LOOKUP, never a scan whose result depends on position. Uniqueness costs nothing here and this is why: per-relation partial absence is ALREADY EXPRESSIBLE INSIDE ONE ENTRY, because AbsentCapability.relationIds is itself a list. A second entry for the same provider would be a second way to say what one entry already says, and two ways to say one thing is the ambiguity this whole ruling exists to remove.

perFieldRuling.residualStatedNOTDECIDED: whether providers and coverageForAbsent must remain disjoint is NOT ruled here. Disjointness holds 4/4 on live bytes and no artifact requires it. A provider that is present for some relations and absent for others is expressible today by listing it in both, and this ruling neither blesses nor forbids that. See declaredUnresolvedDependencies.DUD-V3-3.

theRULEISAPROPERTYNOTALIST.statement: DL-ORD-2. AN ORDERED COLLECTION IN CapabilityManifestV1 IS ORDER-BEARING ONLY IF THIS SCHEMA NAMES IT SO. Position in a JSON array carries no meaning by default, at any depth, in any collection, including collections a later DELIVERY successor adds. TODAY THIS SCHEMA NAMES NONE.
theRULEISAPROPERTYNOTALIST.whyAPROPERTYANDNOTFOURROWS: the four rows above are INSTANCES. Every converged repair in this corpus replaced a list of places with a structural property, and IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md section 7.1 records why: an enumeration goes stale silently in BOTH directions -- its own parked table named nine against a measured class of thirty-three, and three of the nine turned out not to belong. A five-row table here would go stale the first time DELIVERY adds an array. The property does not.
theRULEISAPROPERTYNOTALIST.theEXEMPTIONMECHANISM: exactly evaluation-proof.v8's: one named field, named in the owning schema, exempted in writing. EP8's programOrder names PolicyV2.evaluationOrder and nothing else. DELIVERY's exemption list is empty and an addition to it is a DELIVERY successor's act.
theRULEISAPROPERTYNOTALIST.andTHEREFOREANEWFIELDISSAFEBYDEFAULT: a DELIVERY successor that adds an array to this schema and says nothing gets the set reading, the canonical-order gate and duplicate rejection automatically. The failure mode this closes is a new field silently inheriting whichever reading its first implementer assumed.

theProductQuestionThisDoesNOTDecide.question: should provider PRECEDENCE exist as a product concept -- 'prefer rust-semantic over syntax-all for declares' -- at all?
theProductQuestionThisDoesNOTDecide.disposition: NOT DECIDED HERE, AND NOT DECIDABLE HERE. IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md section 4.4 is what deciding it inside an architecture candidate would look like in hindsight.
theProductQuestionThisDoesNOTDecide.whyTheRULINGABOVEISSTILLNOTAPRODUCTDECIS: because the two questions are separable and only one of them is DELIVERY's data model. 'Does array position carry meaning?' is a wire-format question with a measured answer: nothing reads it, resolved-inputs forbids the only thing it could mean inside PlanId, and both candidate encodings say order-bearing must be NAMED. 'Should precedence exist?' is a product question, and this ruling deliberately leaves it OPEN AND CHEAP TO ANSWER LATER: if product ever wants precedence it is expressed by an EXPLICIT DECLARED FIELD -- a rank, an order list, whatever the product decision names -- and never by array position. Adding that field is a schemaVersion event with a visible cost, which is the correct price for a product decision and is exactly the price array position would NOT have charged.
theProductQuestionThisDoesNOTDecide.theASYMMETRYTHATDECIDESIT: choosing SET forecloses nothing: precedence remains addable as a field. Choosing SEQUENCE forecloses a great deal silently -- it makes every honest release builder's JSON emission order a PlanId input, so two builders that agree on every fact reach two PlanIds, and no vector anywhere in this corpus would catch it. A reversible ruling and an irreversible one are not symmetric, and where the evidence is measured but not conclusive the reversible one is correct.

admission.rule: THREE GATES, ALL BEFORE ENCODING. A value that fails any gate is not a CapabilityManifestV1, is not committed, and has no capabilityManifestId. Nothing is normalised at a consumer, ever.

ADM-TYPE.statement: Every scalar is admitted by EXACT JSON TYPE before its content is compared. schemaVersion is a JSON integer -- a boolean is not an integer, a float is not an integer, a numeric string is not a number -- and every other declared scalar is a JSON string. The type assertion is the gate; content comparison happens only after it passes.
ADM-TYPE.source: IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md section 6 law 18, verbatim in its own terms. Not a restatement for decoration: NEG-TYPE-1 and NEG-TYPE-2 show this recipe is REACHABLE by the class, because CVE1 is total on booleans and on strings and mints a wrong id rather than failing.
ADM-TYPE.andITAPPLIESTOTHISARTIFACTSOWNVECTORS: the two encoders that produced every digest published here reject a boolean BEFORE the integer check, because Python's bool is an int subclass and `isinstance(True, int)` is True. Law 18 defeated C-2 at v3, v5, v6, v7 and v8 successively, each time inside the repair's own self-certification, and the ordering of those two checks is where it would have entered here.
ADM-TYPE.whatITCANNOTDO: a digest cannot police its own input's type. An implementation that coerces 1.0 to 1 before calling the encoder produces the CORRECT id and has still violated law 18. That is why this is an admission gate and not an encoder property, and this artifact does not claim any vector enforces it.

ADM-CLOSED.statement: DL-CLOSED-1. EVERY JSON OBJECT REACHABLE FROM A COMMITTED CapabilityManifestV1 IS CLOSED -- the record itself, every element of every declared collection, every value of every declared map, and every object a later successor adds at any depth carries EXACTLY its declared key set, each key exactly once, with no undeclared member. A reachable object type that declares no key set is inadmissible until it declares one; permissiveness is never the default.
ADM-CLOSED.whyITMATTERSUNDERCVE1: an undeclared key is not silently dropped by CVE1 -- it changes the id. So an open reading is still injective, and the defect is different and worse than loss: a mistyped key ships a manifest that a human reads as unchanged under an id that has moved. Closing the record turns that into a refusal. Executed at NEG-CLOSED-1, with the id an open reading would have minted published beside it.
ADM-CLOSED.changeFromThePredecessor: delivery.v2 declares `closed: true` on CapabilityManifestV1 only. This narrows the two nested records to match. It is a narrowing: every manifest admissible after this change was admissible before.
ADM-CLOSED.whyAPropertyAndNotTwoTypeNames: an independent review found that delivery.v2 closes CapabilityManifestV1 and closes NEITHER of its two children, so a name-reading grammar silently discards an undeclared member and two distinct documents mint one id. REPRODUCED at capabilityManifestIdentity.recordClosure. Closing the two named children would repair today's schema and reopen the hole the first time a third reachable type is added -- which is exactly how this one arrived. The property quantifies over reachability and does not go stale when the schema grows.

ADM-ORDER.statement: DL-ORD-1. Every ordered collection in a COMMITTED CapabilityManifestV1 is already in its declared canonical order -- strictly ascending by the unsigned bytewise comparison of its declared sort key's NFC UTF-8 bytes. A committed manifest that is not is REJECTED, with domainReasonCode RELEASE.CAPABILITY_MANIFEST_NOT_CANONICAL. It is never sorted into shape by a consumer.
ADM-ORDER.theSTRUCTURALPROPERTYTHISBUYS: the canonicalising sort is THE IDENTITY on every value that has an id. Three consequences follow as theorems rather than as claims: (a) the set reading and the sequence reading compute the SAME BYTES on every admitted value, so the choice between them is unobservable downstream and cannot be got wrong by an implementer; (b) decode(encode(x)) == x LITERALLY for every admitted x, so injectivity needs no 'on canonical forms' qualifier; (c) two distinct committed documents carrying one id is INEXPRESSIBLE, because at most one of any two differently-ordered documents is admissible.
ADM-ORDER.whyREJECTANDNOTNORMALISE: silent normalisation is the defect, not the cure. A consumer that sorts is a consumer that turns two logical inputs into one preimage without telling anyone -- the same shape as silently NFC-normalising a string, which resolved-inputs.v2 already forbids in the encoding this recipe uses. Refusing makes the event observable at the boundary where it can still be fixed.
ADM-ORDER.whereCANONICALISATIONISALLOWED: exactly once, in the release builder, on the producer side, BEFORE the id is minted and before the bytes are committed. That is not a normalisation of a committed value; it is how a committed value is produced from an authoring value. NEG-ORD-3 executes it.
ADM-ORDER.andTHISISWHYTHELIVEFIXTURESAREINADMISSIB: MEASURED: all four of delivery.v2#installProfiles.profiles[*].capabilityManifest fail ADM-ORDER as written. That is not a defect in them -- installProfiles is an AUTHORING catalogue, not a release. It is stated because a reader who takes those four objects as committed manifests will compute four ids that this artifact does not publish, and because the alternative -- a rule the live corpus already satisfies -- would have been a rule with no live witness.

whatICHANGE.change: THE COMMITMENT FRAMING. The proposal imports evaluation-proof.v8's typed-component-merkle grammar into DELIVERY. This artifact uses DELIVERY's own stated form: SHA-256(UTF8(domain) || 0x00 || CVE1(value)).
whatICHANGE.whyNOTAPREFERENCE: MEASURED across the corpus's binding heads. Typed-component/merkle framing appears in EVALUATION-PROOF and EVIDENCE. Domain-prefix-plus-canonical-serialisation appears in DELIVERY, C-2, RESOLVED-INPUTS, FACT-PLANE and RETENTION. DELIVERY states the prefix form THREE TIMES IN ITS OWN BYTES -- KeyDescriptor.keyId, wireSchema.commitments.domainRule, and TypeScriptSemanticUniverseKey, the last of which is literally SHA-256(UTF8(domain) || 0x00 || CVE1(closed record)). And c2-plan-stage-schema.v9's planIntentCommitment -- the corpus's one fully converged identity recipe, named in the dispatch as the standard to match -- is SHA-256(UTF8('opensip.plan-intent.v1') || 0x00 || opensip-canonical-json-v1(PlanIntent)), the same form. Adopting the proposal would have given DELIVERY a SECOND canonicalisation, so that manifestId and capabilityManifestId -- two members of one closed PLAN-ID-V1 map -- would be computed by two incompatible grammars inside one artifact. That is the divergence this repair exists to remove, not an aesthetic difference.

DL-CUST-1.statement: THE COMMITTED CAPABILITY MANIFEST IS A RELEASE ARTIFACT. For every ProfileEntry, the CVE1 committedBytes of that profile's CapabilityManifestV1 are a member of ReleaseManifestV1.artifacts as an ArtifactEntry with mediaType 'application/vnd.opensip.capability-manifest.v1' and executable false, and that artifactId is a member of the same ProfileEntry's artifactIds.
DL-CUST-1.whyTHISANDNOTAPOINTERFIELD: because artifactSetRule ALREADY says what happens to release artifacts -- 'artifacts is the exact installable set; unlisted bytes are never executed' -- and ArtifactEntry ALREADY carries sha256, sizeBytes, platformIds and a dependency closure. Making the manifest an artifact gives it custody by falling under a rule that exists, rather than by adding a second custody mechanism beside it. Nothing new is invented; a thing is placed where the existing rule can see it.

DL-CUST-2.statement: THE JOIN IS A CONTENT TEST, NOT A NAME LOOKUP. ProfileEntry.capabilityManifestId is well formed only if the ProfileEntry's artifactIds closure contains EXACTLY ONE ArtifactEntry with the capability-manifest mediaType, and the bytes that ArtifactEntry's sha256 covers recompute, under CAP-MANIFEST-ID-V1, to capabilityManifestId.
DL-CUST-2.whyTHISISTHEREPAIRANDNOTARENAME: the 'profile' versus 'profileId' spelling mismatch is a symptom. Its cause is that the join was supposed to travel through a NAME, and a name-keyed join is exactly what breaks when one side is spelled differently, or is renamed, or is duplicated, or points at the wrong entry with a valid-looking key. A content test cannot be mis-spelled. Under DL-CUST-2 a mis-pointed artifact is not a broken link a checker must go looking for -- it is a DIGEST MISMATCH at the point of use, and the host already refuses.
DL-CUST-2.existenceAndUNIQUENESSAREBOTHREQUIRED: exactly one. Zero means the release commits an id whose bytes it does not carry, which is today's gap. Two means the release carries two candidate manifests for one profile and the join is ambiguous -- a defect that a mere existence test would admit.

DL-CUST-3.statement: THE SPELLINGS DENOTE ONE VALUE. The decoded manifest's `profile` MUST equal the owning ProfileEntry's `profileId`. A release in which they differ is refused.
DL-CUST-3.whyEQUALITYANDNOTARENAME: renaming either key is available and is not taken, for a stated reason: `profile` is INSIDE the CVE1 preimage, so touching it is an identity-affecting edit to a field every published id depends on, made for a cosmetic gain. Stating that the two spellings must hold one value closes the semantic gap at zero identity cost and is mechanically checkable. theHOSTPATHNOWENDTOEND: 1. verify the ReleaseManifestV1 signature and manifestId, unchanged from delivery.v2.
2. select the ProfileEntry for the requested profileId.
3. locate the unique capability-manifest-mediaType ArtifactEntry inside that ProfileEntry's artifactIds closure (DL-CUST-2).
4. verify the artifact bytes against that ArtifactEntry.sha256 -- an obligation ArtifactEntry already carries for every artifact.
5. recompute capabilityManifestId over those exact bytes and compare with ProfileEntry.capabilityManifestId; a mismatch refuses the release.
6. decode CVE1 and run ADM-TYPE, ADM-CLOSED and ADM-ORDER; any failure refuses the release.
7. check the decoded manifest's `profile` equals the ProfileEntry's `profileId` (DL-CUST-3).
8. place the verified capabilityManifestId in PLAN-ID-V1 preimage field 3.

strongestObjectionTheAuthorExpects.objection: YOU CHANGED THE COMMITMENT FRAMING AND THREW AWAY THREE INDEPENDENT REPRODUCTIONS. A candidate's typed-component-merkle recipe had been reproduced twice before you and once by you, at four ids and eight preimages, with no arithmetic error found. You replaced it with arithmetic only you have run, and every published digest in the corpus's capabilityManifestId conversation now moves.
strongestObjectionTheAuthorExpects.theAUTHORSANSWER: it is the right objection and it is only half wrong. Three things are offered against it, and none of them is 'I preferred mine'. FIRST, the reproduction was not discarded -- it was PERFORMED and is published: proposalEvaluation carries every one of the proposal's values, recomputed here under two encoders, matching byte-exactly, together with the statement that its arithmetic is correct. A departure that cannot reproduce what it departs from is not a departure, it is a guess, and that is not the position here. SECOND, the change is not to a different bespoke grammar but to DELIVERY'S OWN, stated three times in the predecessor's bytes and once, in exactly this shape, over a closed record: SHA-256(UTF8(domain) || 0x00 || CVE1(record)). Adopting the proposal would have left DELIVERY computing two members of one closed PLAN-ID-V1 map -- manifestId and capabilityManifestId -- under two incompatible canonicalisations. THIRD, and this is the part that answers the arithmetic worry directly, the new values are not less verified but MORE: CVE1 has a binding-artifact ORACLE. Both encoders reproduce both pinned PLAN-ID-V1 goldens byte-exactly at their declared preimage lengths, which no bespoke grammar in this corpus can offer, because no bespoke grammar has a pinned golden it did not write itself.
strongestObjectionTheAuthorExpects.whatWOULDCHANGETHEAUTHORSMIND: a binding artifact stating that DELIVERY's identities use evaluation-proof.v8's grammar. None exists -- measured: retention-tiers records namespaceOwner pointing at EP's grammar for the identity IT owns, and that is the corpus's only namespace-authority field. What this document adds is that it REPRODUCED the collision before acting rather than transcribing the report, MEASURED that the defect changes shape rather than disappearing under this artifact's own encoding, declined to close two named types in favour of a reachability property because closing two names is how the hole arrived, and stated one executable equation that detects both channels and would have found this one unaided.
